name: Green Drake Cripple
imitates: A green drake emerger stuck half in its nymphal shuck in the surface film; fish it on flatter water during a drake hatch when trout key on struggling duns.
recipe: TMC 5212 #10-12, bent up at the front
Matched blue dun hen hackle tips

steps.text: Bend the front quarter of the hook up about 25-30 degrees with pliers, without over-bending it.
Start the thread at the bend and lay a base back to the hook bend. Tie in a small clump (6-8 fibers) of stacked moose hock as the tail, about half a shank long.
Tie in copper wire, dub a thick tapered brown abdomen up to the kink, then spiral the wire forward in six to eight turns and break it off.
Strip the base of a hen neck feather, tie it in at the front of the abdomen, fold the fibers back and wrap three tight turns. Clip the excess.
Sweep the hackle fibers back with a few thread wraps over its base so it sits wet-fly style, then trim the fibers off the top of the body.
Tie two matched CDC feathers in with opposed tips at the front of the abdomen, splayed away from the body. Clip the butts flush.
Pair two webby hen hackle tips with opposed curves and measure them so they reach just past the CDC tips.
Tie the hen tips in over the front of the abdomen with a pinch wrap and a narrow band of thread.
Clip the butts flush, build a smooth thread base over the stubs and let the hen tips splay over the top.
Pull the near wing down and forward to lie flat along the side, and prop the far wing up, so the wings are deliberately asymmetrical.
Dub the thread with olive superfine and build a blocky thorax from the wing bases forward to one eye length behind the eye.
Finish with bare thread behind the index point, whip finish and clip the thread.
Turn the fly over and trim the hackle from the middle of the underside to expose the abdomen.
The finished Green Drake Cripple, near side view.
